content: What are some traditional Scottish delicacies and where should I try them in Edinburgh?

1. Haggis - a savory pudding made from sheep's offal mixed with spices, oatmeal, and onion that is typically served with neeps and tatties (turnips and potatoes). The best place to try haggis in Edinburgh is at The Royal McGregor located on the Royal Mile.

2. Cullen Skink - a creamy soup made with smoked haddock, potatoes, onions, and cream. The best place to try Cullen Skink in Edinburgh is at The Grain Store located in the old town.

3. Cranachan - a traditional Scottish dessert made with whipped cream, toasted oatmeal, raspberries, and honey. The best place to try Cranachan in Edinburgh is at The Witchery by the Castle.

4. Black Pudding - a type of blood sausage made with pork blood and oatmeal. The best place to try Black Pudding in Edinburgh is at Oink! located in the old town.

5. Scotch Pie - a small pie filled with minced meat, onions, and spices. The best place to try Scotch Pie in Edinburgh is at The Piemaker located on South Bridge.
Yum, those all sound delicious! Do you have any recommendations for vegetarian options in Edinburgh?

Yes, there are several vegetarian options in Edinburgh. Some popular ones include:

1. Vegetarian Haggis - made from vegetables, lentils, and spices instead of offal. The best place to try vegetarian haggis in Edinburgh is at Henderson's Vegan.

2. Neeps and Tatties - the traditional Scottish side dish of turnips and potatoes is vegetarian-friendly and can be found at most Scottish restaurants.

3. Scottish Cullen Skink with Vegetables - a vegetarian version of the traditional Scottish dish, made with a vegetable broth, smoked tofu, and potatoes. The best place to try this dish is at David Bann.

4. Vegetarian Scotch Eggs - a vegetarian version of this classic snack made with a quorn or vegetable sausage wrapped around a boiled egg and coated in breadcrumbs. The best place to try vegetarian Scotch eggs is at The Pakora Bar.

5. Veggie Haggis and Tattie Scone Breakfast - a filling vegetarian breakfast made with vegetarian haggis, tattie scones (potato-based bread), mushrooms, and sautéed spinach. The best place to try this breakfast is at Loudons Cafe and Bakery.
I think I'll try the vegetarian haggis at Henderson's Vegan and the Scottish Cullen Skink with vegetables at David Bann. Can you recommend any good places for a vegan breakfast in Edinburgh?

Yes, here are some great places to try for a vegan breakfast in Edinburgh:

1. Beetroot Sauvage - A vegan café that specializes in plant-based breakfast dishes. Some of their popular options include avocado toast, pancakes, and tofu scramble. 2. Holy Cow - A vegetarian and vegan café that offers a range of breakfast options including tofu scramble, vegan sausages, and vegan tattie scones. 3. Loudons Cafe and Bakery - Offers vegan breakfast options such as a vegan cooked breakfast and vegan porridge with fruit and nut toppings. 4. Seeds for the Soul - A vegan café that offers a range of gluten-free breakfast options such as chia seed pudding, smoothie bowls, and vegan frittatas. 5. The Bluebird Café - Offers a vegan breakfast consisting of avocado toast, scrambled tofu, vegan sausages, and beans. All these cafes are located in central Edinburgh and are a must-visit for vegan breakfast lovers.
Wow, so many great options to choose from! I think I'll start my day with a visit to Beetroot Sauvage for some vegan pancakes.
Enjoy your visit to Beetroot Sauvage and your vegan pancakes, they are truly delicious! Edinburgh has some really great vegan options so you're sure to have a great breakfast experience.
That sounds amazing! Do any of these vegan cafes also offer vegan pastries or baked goods? I have a bit of a sweet tooth.

Yes, most of these vegan cafes offer a range of vegan pastries and baked goods. Here are some of the top places to satisfy your sweet tooth in Edinburgh:

1. Sugar Daddy's Bakery - Offers a range of vegan cupcakes, cakes, and sweets.

2. The Chocolate Tree - A vegan and vegetarian chocolate café that offers a range of handmade chocolates and vegan cakes.

3. Lovecrumbs - A trendy café that offers a variety of vegan cakes, pastries, and sweet treats.

4. Bakery Andante - A bakery that has a range of vegan pastries to choose from including croissants, cinnamon rolls, and Danish pastries.

5. Considerit - Offers a variety of vegan doughnuts and chocolates, made using only the best ingredients and innovative recipes.

These places are just a few of the many bakeries and cafes across Edinburgh that offer vegan pastries and sweets.
Mmm, vegan doughnuts and chocolates sound delicious! I think I'll have to check out Considerit. Thanks for all the recommendations, I can't wait to try them out!

You're welcome! Considerit is a great choice and their vegan doughnuts and chocolates are really popular among locals and visitors alike. Have a great time trying out all these amazing vegan places in Edinburgh!
